newsitem.title: USA: Genzyme, Geltex in RenaGel venture.
newsitem.headline: Genzyme, Geltex in RenaGel venture.

text.p: Genzyme Corp's Genzyme General division said Wednesday it formed a joint venture with GelTex Pharmaceuticals Inc for the final development of a kidney failure treatment called RenaGel.

The deal calls for Genzyme General to pay GelTex $27.5 million, consisting of a $2.5 million equity investment, a $15 million payment on receipt of marketing approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Adminstration, and a $10 million payment one year after FDA approval.
GelTex will contribute RenaGel and the product's underlying patents and technology to the venture, called RenalGel LLC, as well as its expertise in the area of chronic renal failure.
Genzyme General will handle sales, marketing, reimbursement, patient support, and international regulatory activities.

The joint venture will have rights to sell RenaGel, except in Japan and certain Pacific Rim countries. GelTex previously licensed RenaGel development and commercialization rights in those countries to Chugai Pharmaceutical Co Ltd.
Genzyme General and GelTex will share equally all profits and expenses in the venture, including expenses to complete RenaGel's development.

GelTex has completed two Phase III clinical trials of RenaGel in the United States and will submit a new drug application for marketing approval to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in the fourth quarter of 1997. Applications for approval in Europe are scheduled to be filed next year.
